chunks: Fuḍayl ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom! Pray to Allah for me, for verily I have many sins.' So he said, 'Stop, O Abū ʿUbaydah! Let Satan not be a helper of your base-self. Verily the pardon of Allah cannot be compared to anything.'

key_terms.جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a common phrase of respect and devotion)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about Satan and Allah's pardon when asked for forgiveness?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) responds to Abū ʿUbaydah’s plea for intercession by highlighting the psychological mechanism of sin: as long as Satan remains an ally to one's ego (*nafs*), the accumulation of sins persists. The Imam’s assertion that 'Allah's pardon is unlike anything else' underscores the Shia theological emphasis on divine mercy (*rahmah*) being intrinsic and boundless, rather than merely a transactional response to supplication. This highlights the balance between self-accountability (*muhasabah*) and reliance on God's unique capacity to forgive, a core theme in Zuhd (asceticism) literature.
